[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] DartPoints own site describes a strategy of delivering enterprise grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure services to communities outside the largest United States metros, operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 regional markets. The company began operations in the early 2000s. DartPoints is headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas. This session refreshed and sharpened a prior research passes brief note that the company received a strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure in 2025: per both DartPoints own press release and independent trade press corroboration from Data Center Dynamics, both fetched fresh this session, NOVA Infrastructure actually acquired majority control of DartPoints, announced April 30, 2025, with lending partner Orion Infrastructure Capital, committing more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital, while the prior owner, Astra Capital Management, retained a meaningful minority stake. As part of that same transaction, DartPoints acquired the underlying real estate for three of its data centers, in Greenville, South Carolina, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and Asheville, North Carolina, per both sources. DartPoints own site lists 11 facilities across 10 markets, including Baton Rouge, Louisiana (2 facilities) and Shreveport, Louisiana, Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio, Columbus, Indiana, Asheville, North Carolina, and Columbia, Greenville, Charleston, and Spartanburg, South Carolina, matching every state where this registry lists a DartPoints facility, and DCD independently corroborates the same 11 facility, 10 market count and adds that the company serves more than 900 enterprise customers including Fortune 500 companies, universities, and hospital systems. The company emphasizes AI ready, high density infrastructure, 99.999 percent uptime, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. This specific row, DartPoints Baton Rouge 2 (internal code BTR02), per the operators own dedicated location page for this facility, fetched fresh this session, sits at 7139 Florida Blvd, Baton Rouge, LA 70806. This is one of the three facilities, per the NOVA Infrastructure transaction sourcing above, whose underlying real estate DartPoints itself now owns following the April 2025 transaction.

reading.body:
DartPoints Baton Rouge 2 publishes 3 megawatts of IT capacity, making it the largest mapped data center facility in Louisiana and accounting for nearly 40 percent of the state's published data center load.

The facility is one of three DartPoints properties whose real estate the operator acquired outright in April 2025 when NOVA Infrastructure took majority control of the company with more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital. This shift signals sustained investment in regional capacity outside major metropolitan markets. At 3 megawatts, the site holds roughly 75 racks assuming 40 kilowatts per rack, a common density for AI training workloads.

DartPoints operates 11 facilities across 10 regional markets and serves more than 900 enterprise customers including Fortune 500 companies, universities, and hospital systems. The company emphasizes AI-ready infrastructure and high-density deployment. The data does not disclose the facility's total power supply, electrical grid connection capacity, or headroom for expansion beyond the currently published 3 megawatts. Whether this campus can grow depends on factors the operator has not revealed.
